title: Help, Lord, for Men of Virtue Fail
description: Help, Lord, for Men of Virtue Fail in Tonic Solfa to YORK, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 8 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for The Psalms of David Imitated in the Language of the New Testament (1719): Psalm 12, part 2, headed “Complaint of a general corruption of manners; or, The promise and signs of Christ's coming to judgment”.
Watts' psalms were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Common Metre (8.6.8.6). This page sets the words to YORK; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Help, Lord, for men of vir-tue fail, Re-li-gion los-es ground, The sons of vi-o-lence pre-vail, And treach-e-ries a-bound.

lines: Help, Lord, for men of virtue fail,
Their oaths and promises they break,
With fair deceitful lips they speak,
If we reprove some hateful lie,
"Are not our lips our own" they cry,
Where a vile race of men
Is rais'd to seats of power and pride,
And bears the sword in vain.
When faith is hardly to be found,
Is not thy chariot hastening on?
Hast thou not given this sign?
May we not trust and live upon
"Yes," saith the Lord, "now will I rise,
Thy word, like silver seven times try'd,
The men that in thy truth confide,

source: Isaac Watts, The Psalms of David Imitated (1719)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to YORK by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
